title: Grateful Dead Live at 363 6th Street on 1966-01-29

ai_review.summary: A historically quirky Acid Test recording with trippy ambience and decent audio quality, but its appeal lies mainly in novelty rather than musical performance.
ai_review.review: The set captures an oddball acid‑test session featuring a Ken Kesey interview and some loose jams that many fans find "trippy" and historically interesting. Audio is generally clear enough for the era, though several reviewers note the interview’s intrusive nature and question its listening value beyond novelty.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating of 3.9 across eight reviews, with mixed praise for the historic interview and criticism of its relevance; audio is acceptable but not exceptional.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note the recording is clearer than earlier acid tests, though some find the interviewer distracting; no major soundboard or audience issues reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: An Acid Test event blending interview snippets and loose jam segments rather than a conventional concert; the flow feels experimental and novelty‑driven.
